summary:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester.

This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited.

Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

Users who cannot upgrade right away should set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.

PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).

monailabel (aka MONAI Label) before 0.8.6 allows directory traversal, with resultant remote code execution, via the image parameter to the PUT /datastore/image endpoint, as exploited in the wild starting in September 2026.

audio-separator before 0.47.2 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying malicious Demucs .th model files loaded via torch.load with weights_only=False. Local users writing to the shared /tmp/audio-separator-models/ default directory, or attackers controlling unverified model download sources, can execute code when victims run Demucs separation.

MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. Starting in 3.3.0 and prior to 3.15.0, the POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test endpoint (accessible without credentials when server authentication is not enabled) calls _validate_webhook_url() in mlflow/utils/validation.py only for the original URL while mlflow/webhooks/delivery.py follows redirects and re-resolves the hostname without pinning the validated address, allowing attackers to reach internal or cloud metadata services and receive response_status and response_body. The unauthenticated attack scenario described here applies to deployments without authentication. With MLflow’s built-in basic authentication enabled, requests to this endpoint require valid credentials; this issue does not itself bypass authentication. This issue is fixed in version 3.15.0.

Improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in the system plugin daemon in Synology BeeStation OS (BSM) before 1.1-65374 and Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) before 7.2-64570-4, 7.2.1-69057-6 and 7.2.2-72806-1 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via unspecified vectors.

The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the save_single_batch_file function. This is due to a PHP type-juggling authentication bypass via loose != comparison with no is_string() guard, combined with unsanitized base64-decoded path construction in save_single_batch_file() lacking any directory traversal containment. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to execute code on the server. Exploitation requires that the site owner has completed the plugin's initial setup so that the site_type and prod_key_random_id options are non-empty, though any non-empty secret value is bypassable via the type-juggling flaw.

Description:
This issue affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/3. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can cause a use-after-free condition in the NGINX worker process, leading to a restart. Exploitation also depends on conditions beyond the attacker’s control. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy client requests to a backend, a specially crafted request can result in use-after-free in the worker process, if this process is running low on worker_connections. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.




Impact:



This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or may allow a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue occurs when NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a proxy, the proxied server name includes variables, and a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive sends a subrequest to a location that resolves the same server name. Under these conditions, a specially crafted HTTP request may cause a use-after-free condition in a worker process. An attacker may also be able to execute code if Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: 
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or perform remote code execution (RCE)



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Flowise v3.0.1 < 3.0.8, and 3.0.8 < 3.1.3 with 'ALLOW_BUILTIN_DEP' enabled contain an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability and node VM sandbox escape due to insecure use of integrated modules (Puppeteer and Playwright) within the nodevm execution environment. An authenticated attacker able to create or run a tool that leverages Puppeteer/Playwright can specify attacker-controlled browser binary paths and parameters. When the tool executes, the attacker-controlled executable/parameters are run on the host and circumvent the intended nodevm sandbox restrictions, resulting in execution of arbitrary code in the context of the host. This vulnerability was incorrectly assigned as a duplicate CVE-2025-26319 by the developers and should be considered distinct from that identifier.

VMware vCenter contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the VMware Directory Service.
Affected versions: 9.1.x (fixed in 9.1.1.0200); 9.0.x (fixed in 9.0.2.0200); 8.0 (fixed in 8.0 U3m); 5.x (fixed in 5.2.5).
Telco Cloud Platform 3.0, 4.x, 5.0.x, 5.1.x, 5.2 and Telco Cloud Infrastructure 3.0 are also affected (see KB463116).

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a mail proxy, undisclosed traffic can cause a use-after-free in an nginx worker process. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
A remote unauthenticated attacker may crash an nginx worker process or corrupt its memory, disrupting service. Remote code execution is a potential impact. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

The GiveWP – Donation Plugin and Fundraising Platform plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to donor account account takeover in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0. This is due to the plugin not properly validating a donor's identity prior to updating the password of a linked WordPress account. The donation receipt processes an attacker-controlled first name through the V3 template engine and then reprocesses the result through the legacy `{meta_donor_*}` engine, which can disclose the donor's email-access bearer token. The donor-dashboard password endpoint accepts that token by itself and calls `wp_set_password()` for the WordPress user linked to the donor. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to reset the password of any WordPress account linked to a GiveWP donor record and gain access to that account. If the linked account is an administrator, the attacker can achieve full site compromise and remote code execution through standard administrator functionality. A published GiveWP form with a usable gateway, enabled donor email access (enabled by default), knowledge of the donor email address, and an account already linked to the targeted donor record are required. NOTE: This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-82676 to satisfy the administrator donor pre-requisite for a targeted administrator user attack.

ThinkPHP 2.0 through 2.2 and 3.0 Lite mode contains an eval injection vulnerability in the Dispatcher PATH_INFO parsing, which uses preg_replace with the /e modifier and a double-quoted replacement. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted requests to index.php with a malicious 's' parameter containing PHP expressions to execute arbitrary code on the server. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

Traefik versions before v2.11.55 and versions v3.0.0 before v3.7.11 contain an authentication bypass vulnerability in the digestAuth middleware where unknown usernames receive an empty secret instead of rejection. Attackers can compute a valid digest response using the empty secret and arbitrary credentials to bypass authentication on any digestAuth-protected route without a valid username or password.

Traefik versions >= v3.7.0 and < v3.7.11 contain an authentication bypass in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider. The TLS option generated for an Ingress carrying the nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret annotation was named after the Ingress namespace and name. As a result, two Ingress objects sharing the same host, the same client CA secret, and the same client-authentication mode produced two distinct TLS option names for that host. Traefik treats this as a TLS options conflict and falls back to the entry point's default TLS configuration, which does not request a client certificate, so a route configured with nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: "on" becomes reachable without a client certificate. Only the v3.7 line is affected; the issue is fixed in v3.7.11.

knowns through 0.36.1 fails to properly validate template destination paths in the code generation template engine, allowing attackers to read and write arbitrary files outside the project root. Attackers can supply malicious templates that traverse directories to overwrite shell profiles, steal credentials, or achieve persistent code execution on victim systems.

WWBN AVideo 6.5 before 29.8.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to log in as any user via Hybridauth social login display names. Attackers can set their X, Facebook, Yahoo or LinkedIn display name to a victim's username and withhold email, causing login.json.php or oauth2.php to log them in as that account, including administrators, without a password.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to insecure deserialization in the SharePoint Tap MulticastTransceiver component. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code on the affected system.

The urwid web display backend (urwid/display/web.py) generates web session identifiers (urwid_id) in Screen.start() by concatenating two random.randrange(10**9) calls that use Python's Mersenne Twister PRNG, which is not cryptographically secure. Each call consumes approximately 30 bits of PRNG state, and the Mersenne Twister internal state is approximately 19,937 bits, so an attacker who observes approximately 334 session IDs (for example via the X-Urwid-ID HTTP response header) can fully reconstruct the internal state and predict all past and future session IDs (Path B). The same identifier is also used as the filename of a FIFO created in the world-listable /tmp directory (for example /tmp/urwid375487765176907690.in), so any local user on the host can list /tmp to enumerate active session tokens directly (Path A). With a valid session ID, an attacker can read the victim's terminal screen via the polling endpoint, inject keystrokes into the victim's session (yielding OS-level code execution with the session owner's privileges if the session runs a shell), and inject exit sequences or flood the FIFO to terminate or crash the session. A prior Bandit S311 warning on this usage was suppressed with # noqa: S311 rather than fixed

phpMyFAQ versions 3.1.0 before 4.1.7 contain an authentication bypass vulnerability in AuthLdap::create(). When LDAP authentication is enabled, after a successful LDAP bind the code calls User::setStatus('active') unconditionally, which overwrites the account_status column of a pre-existing local account from 'blocked' to 'active'. As a result, a user whose local phpMyFAQ account has been administratively blocked can restore their account and log in by authenticating via LDAP. The state transition is not logged, so administrators cannot detect that the block was overridden. Fixed in 4.1.7.

OpenRemote core before 1.34.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in UserAssetProvisioningMQTTHandler that allows unauthenticated attackers to impersonate provisioned devices without proof of private key possession. Attackers can publish a known device's public certificate to the provisioning request topic, authenticating their anonymous MQTT connection as the device's service account to read and modify assets.

isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.8, git cherry-pick applies tree changes through applyTreeChanges in src/utils/walkerToTreeEntryMap.js without checking whether a leading path component is a symbolic link. If a victim worktree contains a tracked symlink to a location outside the worktree and a cherry-picked tree places a file beneath that path, the write follows the symlink and materializes attacker-controlled blob content at the external destination. This allows arbitrary file writes and can cause data tampering, code injection into interpreted files, privilege escalation, denial of service, or follow-on code execution depending on the selected target path. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.8.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain Administrator role by spoofing X-Forwarded-For through a loopback-trusted reverse proxy. Attackers can send requests with Host set to localhost and X-Forwarded-For set to 127.0.0.1 to read private note-history contents via the /history/*path route when no lock-screen password is set.

The Shortcodes and extra features for Phlox theme plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 2.17.22 via the 'extra_template_path' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The slug-based allowlist introduced as the fix for CVE-2023-37888 constrains only the template_part_file filename suffix and does not validate the extra_template_path directory component, meaning path traversal sequences are fully functional against this parameter.

The Chatterbug Forms – Fast, Flexible WordPress Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the cbforms_delete_uploaded_files function in all versions up to, and including, 1.1 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Exploitation requires an administrator to delete the attacker-planted form entry, and the attacker must know or be able to guess the absolute path of a file writable by the PHP process. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Mega Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder with Multi-Step & Conditional Logic plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the delete_entry function in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.9 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). The attacker-supplied path is stored via the unauthenticated form submission endpoint, but the actual file deletion only occurs when an administrator subsequently deletes the stored entry — a routine housekeeping action that serves as the detonation trigger. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in ImageTransforms::normalizeTransform() that allows attackers to instantiate arbitrary classes by supplying class:null with a __class key. Attackers can reach the method through Craft Commerce's payments/pay redirect template calling customer.photo.getUrl() with a crafted transform to instantiate classes like yii\rbac\PhpManager and execute PHP.

Etherpad is a real-time collaborative editor. From 1.8.14 until 3.3.3, the pre-authentication /static/* plugin asset handler in src/node/utils/Minify.ts performs a backslash-to-forward-slash conversion after src/node/utils/sanitizePathname.ts has completed its POSIX path checks. On POSIX systems the sanitizer correctly treats backslashes as ordinary filename bytes, but the later conversion turns encoded backslash-separated parent-directory segments into traversal components without revalidation or containment. The expressPreSession registration and the always-present ep_etherpad-lite core pseudo-plugin make this path reachable without credentials, allowing a remote attacker to read any file available to the Etherpad process. Disclosed configuration or environment secrets can expose administrator credentials, after which the administrator plugin installer can provide in-process code execution and full server compromise. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.3.

The Charitable – Donation & Fundraising Platform (Donation Forms, Recurring Donations & Fundraising Campaigns) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'stripe_payment_method' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.15.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The nonce required to reach the nopriv AJAX endpoint is publicly obtainable from any rendered campaign donation form, making exploitation trivially accessible to unauthenticated visitors on sites with Stripe configured as a payment gateway.

The Restrictions for BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This is due to the plugin splicing the attacker-controlled request URI into a PHP expression inside a double-quoted string and evaluating it with eval(). Because PHP interpolates double-quoted strings, a payload of the form {${...}} in the URL path is executed during interpolation, so no quote breakout is required and WordPress' slashing does not mitigate it. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server with a single GET request. The affected conditions ship enabled by default and are evaluated before any logged-in check, so no plugin configuration is needed; the site must have BuddyPress and Paid Memberships Pro active alongside this plugin.

Use after free in Views in Google Chrome on on Windows prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker leveraging social engineering to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted Chrome extension. (Chromium security severity: High)

@better-auth/scim (a better-auth plugin) versions >= 1.4.0-beta.27 through <= 1.6.21 and >= 1.7.0-beta.0 through <= 1.7.0-beta.9 contain an authorization bypass. SCIM token issuance did not reject provider IDs already used by existing SSO, SAML, OIDC, generic OAuth, or social account providers, and the same logical provider ID was used for both SCIM provider configuration and account ownership. An authenticated user could mint a SCIM token whose provider ID collided with an existing provider namespace, causing SCIM user routes to resolve account rows the token never provisioned. This allowed listing, reading, updating (including rewriting global profile/email fields without uniqueness checks), and deleting global user accounts and sessions, resulting in account takeover and unauthorized deprovisioning. Fixed in 1.6.22 and 1.7.0-beta.10 (1.7.0-rc.0).

A flaw was found in NetworkManager-iodine, the iodine VPN plugin for NetworkManager. A local unprivileged user can exploit a vulnerability in how the 'nameserver' setting is processed when establishing an iodine VPN connection. By embedding shell metacharacters (special characters that can execute commands) in the 'nameserver' value, an attacker can inject and execute arbitrary commands. These commands run with root privileges before the application drops its elevated permissions, leading to local privilege escalation.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains a local file inclusion in the ESign router (library/ESign/Router.php), which passes the unsanitized module parameter into a require_once of '<module>/Controller.php', and the fax module's faxProcessUploads writes attacker-named files to a predictable temp path without extension checks. Authenticated attackers can upload a PHP file named Controller.php, then request interface/esign/index.php with a traversing module parameter to include it and execute arbitrary code.

Use after free in Extensions in Google Chrome prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker leveraging social engineering to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted Chrome extension. (Chromium security severity: Medium)

Use after free in SignIn in Google Chrome on on Windows prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker leveraging social engineering to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via UI Interaction. (Chromium security severity: Low)
Use after free in DOM in Google Chrome prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a crafted Chrome extension. (Chromium security severity: High)

** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** 



Improper Authentication in Apache SeaTunnel Web 1.0.2 allows a user whose account has been disabled to authenticate with valid credentials and obtain a new login token. The login query does not check the account status, so disabling an account does not prevent new logins or access to protected APIs using the newly issued token. This issue requires valid credentials for the disabled account; it is not a credential-free authentication bypass.



Apache SeaTunnel Web is no longer maintained. The affected 1.0.2 release does not contain the account-status check added to the main branch in pull request #264. There is no maintained fixed release. Users should discontinue use of this unsupported component.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to overwrite pages their per-page permissions deny by abusing FolderStorage key delimiter collisions and PageStorage folder reconstruction. Attackers can rename a folder like locked*** or save from a page with an unusual prefix width through a front-end Flex pages form, replacing protected content and permissions to access the protected subtree.

All versions of LaraDashboard contain an authentication bypass in SocialAuthService::findOrCreateUser(), which links a social login to an existing account by email without checking that the OAuth provider verified that email. Unauthenticated attackers using an OAuth/OIDC provider that asserts a victim's email can log in as any user, including Superadmin, and keep persistent access through a linked social_accounts entry.

Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel vulnerability in miniOrange miniorange otp verification miniorange-otp-verification allows Authentication Abuse.This issue affects miniorange otp verification: from n/a through 5.6.1.

The BuddyBoss Addons plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in versions up to, and including, 1.2.1. This is due to the Social Login REST endpoint trusting unverified Apple and Facebook identity-token claims and linking an attacker-controlled provider identifier to an existing WordPress user selected by the token’s email claim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know a user’s email address to associate their provider identity with that account, including administrator accounts, and subsequently authenticate as the victim. Successful exploitation requires the BuddyBoss Platform plugin to be installed and active, with the Social Login module and selected provider enabled and configured. On sites with the separate BuddyBoss App JWT component, the vulnerable REST request can return an application token immediately.

Grav API plugin from 1.0.0 before 1.1.4 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows publishers with media and page write rights to write theme template files through the blueprint-upload endpoint. Attackers can upload a file into a theme's Twig templates folder and include it from sandboxed page Twig to execute commands as the web-server user.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to a stack-based buffer overflow when processing a specially crafted PROXY protocol v1 header. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability to cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code.

A flaw was found in the Kuadrant WebAssembly (WASM) shim shipped in Red Hat Connectivity Link 1.5. When a TokenRateLimitPolicy is attached to an HTTPRoute that also has an AuthPolicy - or when a RateLimitPolicy with defaults or overrides is attached to the Gateway or listener of such routes - the shim's action pipeline fails to dispatch the authentication guard at request time, and the request is forwarded upstream. Unauthenticated requests return 200 OK instead of 401, and neither authentication nor rate limiting is enforced. Both policies continue to report Enforced, leaving no status-level indication of the failure.

A vulnerability was identified in Gladys Assistant up to 4.71.0. This affects an unknown function of the file gateway.downloadBackup.js of the component Backup Restore Endpoint. The manipulation of the argument file_url leads to os command injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 4.72.0 mitigates this issue. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 8.2.0 until 8.6.5, an unauthenticated attacker can send a WMS GetLegendGraphic request with a nonempty BBOX and repeated LAYER parameters to trigger a heap buffer overflow in msWMSDispatch() in src/mapwms.cpp. The handler appends synthesized entries to cgiRequestObj.ParamNames and cgiRequestObj.ParamValues at NumParams without retaining the arrays' capacity or reallocating them, while incrementing NumParams inside the loop. Once the parser's hidden capacity is exhausted, the writes pass the heap allocation boundary. A single request can corrupt heap memory and crash the process; code execution may be possible but was not demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

LiveBOS builds through 2023-08-16 contain a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files via the imgName parameter in /feed/ShowImage.do using a ';.js.jsp' suffix bypass. Attackers can send crafted GET requests with directory traversal sequences in imgName to read system files such as /etc/passwd. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-30.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java treats a complete field line that ends exactly at a known field-section boundary as incomplete and returns without consuming bytes. BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection then leaves fieldSectionLength unchanged and repeats the loop because its forward-progress checks are Java assertions, which are normally disabled in production. A remote peer that sends a known-length Binary HTTP header or trailer section ending at that boundary can make the parser spin indefinitely and pin the Netty event-loop or worker thread responsible for the channel. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java loops while fieldSectionLength is nonzero and relies on disabled-by-default assertions to require BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine to return a value and consume bytes. A corrupt field line can consume more bytes than its understated declared section length and drive the counter negative, or a truncated field line can return without consuming data and leave the parser in the same state. An unauthenticated OHTTP peer can encrypt such Binary HTTP content under the gateway public configuration, reach OHttpRequestResponseContext.ContentDecoder.decodeChunk, and permanently pin a Netty event-loop thread at full CPU before application business logic. Multiple requests can exhaust the event-loop group and deny service until restart. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.
Improper Validation of Unsafe Equivalence in Input vulnerability in Liquid Web / StellarWP GiveWP give allows Authentication Bypass.This issue affects GiveWP: from n/a through 4.16.9.

The Mang Board plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.7. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete any board post — including administrator-owned content — along with its associated comments and file links. A nonce sufficient to pass the initial nonce check is publicly exposed on any board listing page, meaning no prior authentication or privileged access is required to initiate the exploit.

A security flaw has been discovered in Gladys Assistant up to 4.71.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file server/lib/gateway/gateway.downloadBackup.js of the component Backup Restore Handler. The manipulation results in path traversal. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 4.72.0 will fix this issue. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

uproot dynamically generates Python class source code from ROOT TStreamerInfo records in a file and compiles it at runtime. Some file-controlled streamer metadata fields (for example, streamer element names) are interpolated into the generated Python source without safe quoting via repr() or the !r format specifier. An attacker who can supply a crafted ROOT file can place Python expression-breaking content into a streamer metadata field. When uproot generates and invokes the corresponding reader method, the injected Python expression is evaluated in the context of the process opening the file, resulting in arbitrary Python code execution in applications that open or process attacker-controlled ROOT files with affected uproot code paths.

The Grav API plugin (getgrav/grav-plugin-api) versions >= 1.0.6 and < 1.0.13 contain a privilege escalation vulnerability. A scoped API key minted on a super-admin account bypasses its declared scope cap on four isSuperAdmin()-gated write endpoints (in GroupsController, AccountsConfigController, PreferencesController, and DashboardWidgetController). These endpoints authorize via a super-admin early-return that never invokes requirePermission()—the sole enforcement point of the scope cap—so a 'read-only'-scoped key (e.g. api.pages.read) can perform super-only write operations, including rewriting group ACL maps to grant super-admin privileges to arbitrary accounts. A leaked or delegated read-only CI/monitoring key can therefore gain full super-admin write capability. Fixed in 1.0.13.

Ghostscript before 10.08.0 contains a -dSAFER bypass vulnerability in the .putgstringcopy procedure in gs_fonts.ps, which calls the privileged .forceput operator without checking operand types. Attackers can supply crafted PostScript or PDF documents that trigger a type error, recover .forceput via a custom error handler, and cause a use-after-free across save/restore to execute arbitrary code.

The CWILL (Formerly ParcelPanel) – Shipment Tracking, Tracking & Order Tracking for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[].courier_code, data[].tracking_number (plus pp_sign for the auth bypass)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.6.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The authentication bypass is reachable only when the parcelpanel_api_key WordPress option is non-empty, which occurs automatically once an admin has opened or connected the ParcelPanel admin page; at that point any unauthenticated attacker can bypass the sole access gate by supplying a JSON boolean true as pp_sign, which PHP's loose == operator coerces to true when compared against the non-empty md5 hex string.

The targets R package before 1.12.1 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run arbitrary R code by planting format functions in the data store metadata file. Attackers can supply a crafted _targets data store whose custom format or CAS repository functions are passed to eval(parse()), executing code when victims call tar_read(), tar_load() or tar_workspace().

diffpy.structure before 3.5.1 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run Python code by supplying crafted CIF symmetry operations passed to eval() in get_symop(). Attackers can embed expressions in the _space_group_symop_operation_xyz or _symmetry_equiv_pos_as_xyz loop to execute code with victim privileges when the CIF file is parsed locally.

llama.cpp b11003 before b12556 contains an integer overflow in the hrm_text loader load_arch_hparams() that allows attackers to bypass the block count check using crafted GGUF metadata. Attackers can supply a GGUF model whose layer factors wrap modulo 2^32, causing load_arch_tensors() to write tensor pointers past model.layers, corrupting heap memory and potentially enabling code execution.

G DATA Total Security TSNxGService Link Following Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of G DATA Total Security. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the TSNxGService service. By creating a symbolic link, an attacker can abuse the service to delete a file. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-28663.

SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to shadow protected $access, $auth, and $token variables by binding them as FOR loop variables. Attackers can wrap queries in nested FOR loops with forged values to satisfy table permission predicates, enabling unauthorized reads, modifications, or deletions as a VIEWER.

A vulnerability was identified in D-Link DIR-600L 2.17b02. Affected is the function genacgi_main of the file gena.cgi of the component GENA Handler. Such manipulation leads to os command injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

n8n before 1.123.89, 2.0.0 before 2.45.5, 2.46.0 before 2.46.1, and 3.0.0 before 3.0.1 contains an insufficient isolation vulnerability in workflow expression evaluation that allows authenticated users to escape the sandbox. Attackers with permission to create or modify workflows can craft expressions referencing unexpected JavaScript properties to execute arbitrary code on the n8n host.

In the nrfconnect/ncs-zigbee repository, the GitHub Actions workflow
.github/workflows/build_documentation.yml used the pull_request_target trigger
while checking out and executing untrusted pull request code. This allowed a
pull request from a fork to run attacker-controlled code in the base repository
context with a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: write, pages: write,
pull-requests: write), enabling remote code execution in CI, token
exfiltration, and unauthorized modification of repository content and GitHub
Pages. The workflow was disabled and then rewritten to remove the issue.

The WP Fastest Cache – WordPress Cache Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary directory deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the singleDeleteCache function in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Successful exploitation requires either the Custom Permalinks plugin or the GeoDirectory plugin to be co-installed, as these provide the necessary mechanism to write a traversal-bearing permalink value into the database that WP Fastest Cache then consumes without validation.

G DATA Total Security Backup Service Uncontrolled Search Path Element Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of G DATA Total Security. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the Backup Service. The service restores archives from an unsecured location. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-28666.

Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the Documents & Files renameFile() action that allows authenticated users with folder upload rights to move files outside adm_my_files by supplying ../ sequences in adm_new_name. Attackers can relocate an uploaded SVG containing script to the web root, where it is served inline and executes stored cross-site scripting against administrators for account takeover.

The affected products have an unauthenticated command injection, which may allow an in-range BLE device to gain access to write to the control interface and influence braking with no authentication or pairing.

SurrealDB from 2.2.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in Document::purge_references that lets authenticated users bypass target table PERMISSIONS by triggering REFERENCE ON DELETE cascades. Attackers can delete a referenced record to delete, unset, or run CUSTOM expressions on referencing records despite PERMISSIONS FOR delete or update NONE.

A vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker with network access to a Cisco Expressway device to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root.

This vulnerability is due to the use of persistent cookies. Additionally, there is insufficient validation of client certificates when the TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, which means that client certificates are not validated. An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device.
Note: Cisco Expressway Series refers to Cisco Expressway Core (Expressway-C) devices and Cisco Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command (OS Command Injection) vulnerability in livebook-dev livebook allows command injection into generated deployment setup commands.

LivebookWeb.Hub.Teams.DeploymentGroupAgentComponent.docker_instructions/2 and LivebookWeb.Hub.Teams.DeploymentGroupAgentComponent.fly_instructions/4 in lib/livebook_web/live/hub/teams/deployment_group_agent_component.ex interpolate deployment group environment variable values into the generated Docker and Fly.io setup commands without shell escaping. The values originate from the deployment group configuration and reach the sinks through Livebook.Hubs.Dockerfile.online_docker_info/3.

Both sinks place the value inside a double-quoted shell word, so a value containing a command substitution such as $(...) or backticks is evaluated by the shell without any need to break out of the quoting, and a literal double quote terminates the quoted word and allows arbitrary further tokens. The generated command is displayed in the Livebook web interface with a copy button, so a user who copies it and runs it without reviewing it first executes the injected commands on their own machine, under their own account.

An attacker requires privileges sufficient to set deployment group environment variables, while the resulting code execution occurs on the machine of whoever runs the generated command. The Kubernetes instructions are not affected, because they render the same values into a YAML manifest with escaping rather than into a shell command.

This issue affects livebook: from 0.13.0 before 0.18.7 and from 0.19.0 before 0.19.9.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in its public shared-view relation endpoints, which verify that a parent record exists but not that it passes the view's row filters. Unauthenticated attackers holding a public share link can supply guessable auto-incrementing ids of filtered-out records to has-many, many-to-many, one-many, or link endpoints to read their child records.

The King Addons for Elementor – 100+ Elementor Widgets, 4 000+ Elementor Templates, WooCommerce Builder, Mega Menu, Popup Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 51.1.89. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary post meta values — including private contact data, API keys, license keys, and plugin-internal metadata — for any published post by supplying an arbitrary meta key name via the unauthenticated AJAX endpoint. The nonce check present in the handler provides no effective barrier because the nonce is emitted into every front-end page for logged-out visitors via wp_localize_script.

Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in Erlang OTP public_key (pubkey_ocsp module) allows OCSP designated-responder authorization bypass via missing signature verification.

The OCSP response validation in public_key:pkix_ocsp_validate/5 does not verify that a CA-designated responder certificate was cryptographically signed by the issuing CA. Instead, it only checks that the responder certificate's issuer name matches the CA's subject name and that the certificate has the OCSPSigning extended key usage. An attacker who can intercept or control OCSP responses can create a self-signed certificate with a matching issuer name and the OCSPSigning EKU, and use it to forge OCSP responses that mark revoked certificates as valid.

This affects SSL/TLS clients using OCSP stapling, which may accept connections to servers with revoked certificates, potentially transmitting sensitive data to compromised servers. Applications using the public_key:pkix_ocsp_validate/5 API directly are also affected, with impact depending on usage context.

This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/public_key/src/pubkey_ocsp.erl and program routines pubkey_ocsp:is_authorized_responder/3.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 27.0 before OTP 27.3.4.10 and OTP 28.4.2, corresponding to public_key from 1.16 before 1.17.1.2 and 1.20.3, and ssl from 11.2 before 11.2.12.7 and 11.5.4.

ILIAS before 9.25, 10.13, and 11.6 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in ilPRGAssignmentFilter::toConditions() that allows authenticated users to inject SQL through the StudyProgramme members list Name and Status filters. Attackers holding only the OrgUnit permission to view members can break out of LIKE literals and execute stacked statements, such as overwriting the root password hash to gain administrative control.

Kan 0.5.5 through 0.7.0 contains an unauthenticated server-side request forgery vulnerability in the /api/download/attatchment route due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-32255. When S3_ENDPOINT is unset, attackers can pass arbitrary url query parameters to fetch() to read internal services, localhost ports, and cloud instance metadata.

OpenCATS before 0.10.0 contains a sql injection vulnerability in the sortDirection parameter of the DataGrid component that allows authenticated users to extract database contents. Attackers can inject malicious SQL via the sortDirection parameter in ajax/getDataGridPager.php to perform time-based blind injection attacks and read sensitive data.

The Video & Photo Gallery for Ultimate Member plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion in versions up to, and including, 1.1.4 This is due to the um_gallery_add_videos() AJAX handler persisting user-supplied videos[] values into the file_name column after only esc_url() — which preserves path-traversal sequences — and the companion um_gallery_delete_photo() helper passing that stored value to unlink() through get_user_image_path() with no canonicalization or allowed-directory check. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can be leveraged to achieve remote code execution when the right file (such as wp-config.

Baidu UEditor 1.4.0 before 1.4.3.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to make arbitrary requests via the source[] parameter in /ueditor/jsp/controller.jsp?action=catchimage. Attackers can supply crafted URLs that the ImageHunter component fetches through url.openConnection() to reach internal services and bypass network restrictions. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-07-03.

Improper path validation vulnerability in the Gleam compiler's handling of git dependencies allows arbitrary file system modification during dependency download.

Dependency names from gleam.toml and manifest.toml are incorporated into filesystem paths without sufficient validation or confinement to the intended dependency directory, allowing attacker-controlled paths (via relative traversal such as ../ or absolute paths) to target filesystem locations outside that directory. When resolving git dependencies (e.g. via gleam deps download), the computed path is used for filesystem operations including directory deletion and creation.

This vulnerability occurs during the dependency resolution and download phase, which is generally expected to be limited to fetching and preparing dependencies within a confined directory. A malicious direct or transitive git dependency can exploit this issue to delete and overwrite arbitrary directories outside the intended dependency directory, including attacker-chosen absolute paths, potentially causing data loss. In some environments, this may be further leveraged to achieve code execution, for example by overwriting git hooks or shell configuration files.

This issue affects gleam: from 1.9.0-rc1 before 1.15.4 and from 1.16.0-rc1 before 1.16.0-rc2.

A flaw was found in the ContentRepositoryImpl.copyExplodedContent function of the wildfly-core library, which is used by WildFly and JBoss EAP to manage server deployments. The issue occurs when the library processes an unsanitized deployment name. Due to a missing containment check, an attacker with the Deployer RBAC role can use path traversal sequences to access files outside the restricted deployment directory. This can allow the attacker to delete arbitrary directories or create files with arbitrary content, leading to a full privilege escalation to the management SuperUser role.

FineCMS versions 5.0.4 before 5.0.11 contain an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the data2 API action handled by list_tag in libraries/Template.php. Attackers can send GET requests to index.php?c=api&m=data2 with a valid auth hash and the param action=sql sql='...' to execute arbitrary SELECT queries and extract database information. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

Chamilo LMS 1.11.10 before 1.11.16 contains an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the searchOptionsFromTags function through the options parameter of extra_field.ajax.php. Attackers can send POST requests with a malicious JSON options array to inject SQL into the IN clause and extract database information. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

CmsEasy 7.7.5_20210919 contains an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the execsql_action function at /?case=crossall&act=execsql that executes attacker-supplied queries decrypted with the hardcoded key 'cmseasy_sql'. Attackers can send a crafted 'sql' parameter to run arbitrary SQL and dump the admin username and password hash. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-22.

Azon Dominator releases through 2024-06-03 contain an SQL injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to manipulate database queries through the cid parameter in /fetch_products.php. Attackers can send crafted POST requests with boolean-based or time-based blind payloads to extract sensitive database information. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-07-30.

SurrealDB 3.1.0 before 4.0.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server because the identifier validator (consume_backtick_ident and validate_identifier) treats the first backtick as the closing delimiter, ignoring escape characters that the SurrealQL parser honors. Attackers can supply MCP tool arguments containing an escaped backtick to break out of the quoted identifier and execute arbitrary SurrealQL statements.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in direct filesystem buckets because BucketController::check_permission evaluates key-based ACLs against the un-normalized object key, while FileStore::to_os_path collapses '..' sequences without a traversal check. An authenticated tenant permitted only for certain keys can supply a key such as /public/../private/confidential.txt to read, write, or delete arbitrary files within the storage root.

OpenCATS from version 0.9.1a before 0.10.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in DataGrid filter handling that allows authenticated attackers to inject SQL through crafted filters targeting the non-filterable Tags column in the Candidates DataGrid. Attackers can bypass column filterable restrictions by manipulating filter requests to execute arbitrary SQL queries against the database.

Worklenz through 3.4.2 fails to properly validate the sort-field query parameter in pagination helper functions, allowing authenticated users to inject arbitrary PostgreSQL expressions into ORDER BY clauses. Attackers can use time-based and boolean-based blind SQL injection techniques to extract sensitive database content including password hashes from other tenants. This is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-25947.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows any authenticated core user to inject SQL by supplying crafted patient_data field names to the CCR revandapprove controller. Attackers can embed scalar subqueries in the UPDATE patient_data SET clause to read staff password hashes and portal reset values, alter arbitrary patient demographics, and take over patient-portal accounts.

Bio-Formats versions before 8.5.0 contain an XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability in the Leica Microsystems metadata parsing component (e.g., XLEF). The parser uses an insecurely configured DocumentBuilderFactory when processing Leica XML-based metadata files, allowing external entity expansion and external DTD loading. A crafted metadata file can trigger outbound network requests (SSRF), access local system resources where readable, or cause a denial of service during XML parsing.

Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') vulnerability in Jacob N. Breetvelt WP Photo Album Plus wp-photo-album-plus allows Remote Code Inclusion.This issue affects WP Photo Album Plus: from n/a through 9.3.06.003.

knowns through 0.36.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the POST /api/embedding-models/test endpoint that issues outbound requests to caller-supplied destinations without validation. Attackers can enumerate internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints by observing transport error messages that reveal network reachability information.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to make the server send HTTP requests by registering an OAuth2 client with an unvalidated jwks_uri. Attackers can trigger the fetch via the token introspection endpoint with an unsigned client_assertion to probe internal services and reach cloud metadata endpoints.

mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.8.5, ssh_backup_create, ssh_backup_restore, ssh_backup_schedule, and ssh_backup_list build remote shell commands from caller-controlled values in src/backup-manager.js and inline backup handlers in src/index.js without neutralizing shell metacharacters. Crafted database, connection, backup directory, path, exclusion, schedule, or comment arguments can therefore execute arbitrary OS commands on managed remote servers as the configured SSH user. ssh_backup_schedule can persist execution through cron. ssh_backup_list does not pass through the server policy check and remains available in readonly and restricted modes, allowing command execution despite those restrictions. Tool arguments can be supplied by a malicious or compromised MCP client or steered through indirect prompt injection; fully trusted benign arguments do not trigger the issue. The earlier database-helper remediation for CVE-2026-77383 applied shell quoting to src/database-manager.js but did not cover these parallel backup builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.5.
